subject: comp
source: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 syllabus 2026–2028, Cambridge International

weeks.topic: Number systems: binary, denary and hexadecimal conversions
objectives: Convert between binary, denary and hexadecimal
Explain why computers use binary

weeks.topic: Uses of hexadecimal; binary addition and overflow
objectives: Describe uses of hexadecimal such as MAC addresses and colour codes
Add 8-bit binary numbers and identify overflow

weeks.topic: Logical binary shifts and two's complement
objectives: Perform left and right logical shifts
Represent negative integers in two's complement

weeks.topic: Representing text: ASCII and Unicode character sets
objectives: Explain how characters are represented in binary
Compare ASCII and Unicode

weeks.topic: Representing sound: sample rate and sample resolution
objectives: Explain how sound is sampled and stored
Describe the effect of sample rate and resolution on quality and size

weeks.topic: Representing images: pixels, resolution and colour depth
objectives: Explain how bitmap images are stored
Describe the effect of resolution and colour depth

weeks.topic: Data storage units and file size calculations
objectives: Use units from bit to exbibyte
Calculate image and sound file sizes

weeks.topic: Data compression: lossy and lossless methods
objectives: Explain why compression is needed
Compare lossy and lossless compression including run-length encoding

weeks.topic: Data transmission: packets and packet switching
objectives: Describe the structure of a packet
Explain how packet switching works

weeks.topic: Transmission methods: serial, parallel, simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex and USB
objectives: Compare serial and parallel transmission
Describe simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex and the USB interface

weeks.topic: Error detection: parity, checksum, echo check, check digit and ARQ
objectives: Explain why errors occur during transmission
Describe methods of error detection

weeks.topic: Encryption: symmetric and asymmetric
objectives: Explain the purpose of encryption
Compare symmetric and asymmetric encryption

weeks.topic: Algorithm design: the program development life cycle and decomposition
objectives: Describe analysis, design, coding and testing
Decompose problems into inputs, processes, outputs and storage

weeks.topic: Representing algorithms: flowcharts and pseudocode
objectives: Use standard flowchart symbols
Write simple algorithms in pseudocode

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: data representation, transmission and algorithm design
objectives: Consolidate conversions and file size calculations
Practise exam-style explanation questions

weeks.topic: Computer architecture: CPU, von Neumann model and fetch–decode–execute cycle
objectives: Describe the role of the ALU, CU, registers and buses
Explain the fetch–decode–execute cycle

weeks.topic: CPU performance, instruction sets and embedded systems
objectives: Explain how cores, cache and clock speed affect performance
Describe embedded systems with examples

weeks.topic: Input and output devices
objectives: Describe how common input and output devices work
Choose devices for given scenarios

weeks.topic: Sensors and their applications
objectives: Identify types of sensors and the data they capture
Choose sensors for monitoring and control

weeks.topic: Primary storage: RAM, ROM and virtual memory
objectives: Compare RAM and ROM
Explain the purpose of virtual memory

weeks.topic: Secondary storage: magnetic, optical, solid-state and cloud storage
objectives: Explain how magnetic, optical and solid-state storage work
Evaluate cloud storage

weeks.topic: Network hardware: NIC, MAC address, IP address and router
objectives: Describe the role of a NIC and MAC address
Compare IPv4 and IPv6 and static and dynamic addresses

weeks.topic: Software: system software, application software and the operating system
objectives: Distinguish system and application software
Describe the functions of an operating system

weeks.topic: Interrupts, firmware and running applications
objectives: Explain how interrupts are generated and handled
Describe the role of firmware and the bootloader

weeks.topic: Programming languages, translators and IDEs
objectives: Compare high-level and low-level languages
Compare compilers, interpreters and assemblers; describe IDE features

weeks.topic: Programming concepts: variables, constants, data types, input and output
objectives: Declare variables and constants with suitable data types
Write programs that use input and output

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: Computer Science Terms 1–2
objectives: Sit timed theory questions on data, hardware and software
Identify topics for follow-up

weeks.topic: Selection: IF and CASE statements
objectives: Write algorithms using IF…THEN…ELSE
Use CASE statements for multiple options

weeks.topic: Iteration: count-controlled, pre-condition and post-condition loops
objectives: Write FOR, WHILE and REPEAT…UNTIL loops
Choose the appropriate loop type

weeks.topic: Totalling, counting and string handling
objectives: Use totalling and counting in algorithms
Use string operations: length, substring, upper and lower

weeks.topic: Arithmetic, logical and Boolean operators; nested statements
objectives: Use arithmetic, comparison and Boolean operators
Write nested selection and iteration

weeks.topic: Validation and verification
objectives: Write range, length, type, presence, format and check-digit validation
Describe double entry and visual check verification

weeks.topic: Test data and trace tables
objectives: Choose normal, abnormal, extreme and boundary test data
Complete trace tables to test algorithms

weeks.topic: Standard algorithms: linear search and bubble sort
objectives: Write a linear search
Write and trace a bubble sort

weeks.topic: Standard algorithms: maximum, minimum and average
objectives: Find maximum and minimum values in a list
Calculate averages using totalling

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: Year 10 Computer Science
objectives: Sit theory and algorithm papers on Year 10 content
Write pseudocode under timed conditions

weeks.topic: Year 10 review and preview of arrays and the internet
objectives: Correct exam errors
Preview arrays and internet technologies
